name: Q. Camurius Q. f. Lem. Numisius Iunior
rank_in_IX: tr(ibunus) [mil(itum)] (the word laticlavius is NOT on the stone; a IIIvir monetalis, so a laticlave is implied)
inscription_ref: CIL XI 5670 (Attidium, Umbria), with CIL XI 5671-5672; AE 1994, +588; AE 2006, +243; AE 2008, +499

CIL XI 5671: Q(uinto) Camurio [- f(ilio)] / Lem(onia) Numi[sio] / Iuniori III[vir(o) ---]

fixed_points.event: a Q. Numisius Iunior consul suffect (with M. Annius Libo)
fixed_points.evidence: Eck, Chiron 2 (1972) 459-62 (diploma from Moesia Superior); de.wikipedia; Eck 2013, 80

fixed_points.event: the career on the stone stops at the legateship of VI Victrix - no consulship; the stone was set up by his children ('...et Iunior patri'), i.e. before any consulship

implied_service_in_IX.earliest: c. 105 (if the tribune is the father of the consul of 161)
implied_service_in_IX.latest: c. 143 (if the tribune is himself the consul of 161)
implied_service_in_IX.most_likely: disputed: c. 139-143 (Eck 1972, A. Birley 1981, Alfoldy 1977) vs. c. 105-120 (Keppie 1989, Hodgson 2021)

reasoning: If tribune = cos. 161: consul at c. 40-42 => born c. 119-121, IIIvir at 18-20 (c. 138-140), tribune c. 139-143 (Eck: 'nicht vor etwa 140/141'; tribunates could last up to 3 years); praetor c. 150, two legionary commands c. 152-158 (Alfoldy), then one post, consul 161. If the dedicating son 'Iunior' is the consul of 161 (Keppie), the father was born c. 85-95 and tribune c. 105-118; his command of VI Victrix could then have been on the Rhine or in Britain c. 125-135. The stone reads 'leg(ionis) VIIII Hi[' - the numeral VIIII is on the stone (not restored); no reading dispute about the numeral was found in EDCS, Eck 1972 or Campbell (blog 2025, who lists it among the 'VIIII HISP' spellings).
scholars_views: Eck 1972: tribune not before c. 140/141, so the legion existed under Antoninus Pius and probably perished at Elegeia 161 (E. Birley's suggestion); A. Birley 1981, 255: tribunate in the 140s, VI Victrix command mid-150s; Alfoldy 1977: praetor c. 150; Keppie 1989, 251-2: the consul of 161 may be the SON of the tribune, who served a generation earlier; Hodgson 2021: follows Keppie (consul = son or grandson); Graafstal 2025 n.19 accepts Keppie; Campbell 2018 calls the consul 'a new discovery, Quintus Numisius Junior' (blurb) and keeps a mid-120s to mid-160s window.
verified_online: Latin verified EDCS (both stones); consular diploma via Eck 1972 PDF (online) and de.wikipedia

reasoning: Four centurionates follow the Dacian-war decoration; at the average c. 3.3 years per post (Graafstal 2025, Table 1, which includes Proclus) the Ninth post falls c. 116-120 and his discharge c. 120 (+/-5). fixed_points.event: VI Victrix moves from Germania Inferior to Britain

reasoning: No fixed point; the sequence IX -> III Aug. -> VI Victrix suggests a Hadrianic career; if the VI Victrix post was in Britain (after 122) the Ninth post is earlier. Note the stone-cutter's VIII: a caution when numerals are used as evidence.

name: Aelius Asclepiades, natione Cilix
rank_in_IX: miles leg. IX (8 years' service, died aged 42)
inscription_ref: CIL X 1769 (Puteoli)
latin_text: D(is) M(anibus) / Aelius Asc/lepiades nati(one) / [C]il(ix) mil(es) leg(ionis) IX / vix(it) ann(os) XXXXII / mil(itavit) ann(os) VIII / Aelia Seleria / b(ene) m(erentibus) f(ecit)  [EDCS text; EDCS dates 141-160 on formula]

fixed_points.event: nomen Aelius = citizenship from Hadrian (117-138) or descendant of such a grant

implied_service_in_IX.most_likely: if a Hadrianic new citizen: enlistment c. 117-130, service to c. 125-138; otherwise no terminus

reasoning: Cited by Bogaers/Eck as a possible Hadrianic recruit (Cilician - hence perhaps enlisted when the legion was in the East). Objections: no praenomen (Keppie 1989, 252-3; Hodgson 2021, 18-19: cannot be shown to have received citizenship himself under Hadrian), 'leg. IX' without cognomen, D.M. formula could be Antonine; Jarrett & Mann 1970, 185 already rejected the inference. Even on the most favourable reading (citizenship 117, enlistment at once) his eight years end c. 125-126 (RAT commentator).
scholars_views: Bogaers 1967, 73 (pro); Jarrett & Mann 1970, 185 (contra); Eck 1972 n.7 (cautious); Keppie 1989, 252-3 (contra); Hodgson 2021, 18-19 (contra).
